name: Oakridge
source: invented example written for calibration, October 2026
agreedBy: Proposed by agentic-rig, to be confirmed by Anthony Stevenson

input.delivery: Oakridge makes bespoke shopfitting joinery: counters, display units and wall systems for independent retailers, each one designed and built for that shop. One job takes two joiners between three and six weeks in the workshop plus two days on site to fit. Nothing is repeated between jobs; every piece is drawn from scratch.
input.pricing: Every job is quoted on hours. We estimate the joiner hours, multiply by 85 CAD an hour, and add materials at cost plus 12 percent. A typical shop fit is 48,000 CAD. No fixed prices, no catalogue, no subscription.
input.cost: Eight joiners at about 78,000 CAD a year each fully loaded. Margin is about 14 percent and it has fallen for three years because overtime rises every time we take on more work than the workshop can hold, and overtime is paid at time and a half while the quote assumed the standard rate.
input.renewal: About a fifth of clients come back, usually when they open a second shop two or three years later. There is no tiering and no way to buy more from us other than another full job. The only plan we have for growth is to hire more joiners, and we have been trying to find two for eight months.

note: The unit is joiner hours (people-bound), two joiners serve one client at a time, margin is thin at 14 percent and eroding through overtime, a fifth of clients return with no expansion path, value per unit is fixed by the hours quoted, and the only named lever is more headcount. Weighted score 32, grade 2.
